generation_meta_data.title: Security: Update vulnerable dependencies in ML evaluation framework
generation_meta_data.description: Security scan flagged several vulnerable packages in requirements.txt. Need to update numpy, torch, and related ML dependencies to address CVE-2024-1234 and others.

generation_meta_data.message: Starting dependency updates for security fixes. Will update numpy from 1.23.5 to 1.24.0, torch from 1.12.1 to 1.13.1, and several others. Should be straightforward - running tests now.
Dependency updates pushed to main. All standard tests passing. Updated requirements.txt with latest secure versions: numpy==1.24.0, torch==1.13.1, scikit-learn==1.3.2
Pulled latest main and ran NLP evaluations on GPT models - everything looks good! Text classification and language modeling evals all passing. Nice work on the security updates.
Having issues with computer vision evaluations after the dependency updates. Getting weird tensor shape errors in CLIP and vision transformer evals. Anyone else seeing this?
@bob Interesting - NLP evals work fine but CV evals broken? That suggests the issue might be in the vision-specific dependencies or tensor operations.

generation_meta_data.title: BUG: Computer vision evaluations failing after dependency updates
generation_meta_data.description: CV evaluations throwing tensor shape errors after security dependency updates. NLP evaluations work fine. Affects CLIP, vision transformers, and image classification models. Error: 'RuntimeError: Expected tensor of shape [224, 224, 3] but got [224, 224, 3, 1]'

generation_meta_data.message: @bob I can help debug this. Let me clone the repo and test different model architectures locally to narrow down which specific operations are failing.

Cloned and testing locally. The issue seems specific to certain CUDA tensor operations. ResNet models work fine, but Vision Transformers and CLIP models consistently fail. Created branch 'debug-cv-deps' to test different package combinations.
I can take a look at the CUDA side of this. Setting up local environment with CUDA 11.7 to reproduce the tensor errors. Will create branch 'cuda-debug' for testing.

Found it! The numpy 1.24.0 update changed how CUDA tensor operations handle memory layout. Older CUDA ops expect contiguous memory but numpy 1.24.0 sometimes returns non-contiguous arrays. Testing with numpy==1.23.5 on my cuda-debug branch.
@charlie That makes perfect sense! Vision models use more complex tensor operations than NLP models. Can confirm - downgrading to numpy 1.23.5 fixes the CV eval issues on my debug-cv-deps branch.
So we need numpy 1.23.5 for CUDA compatibility but numpy 1.24.0 for security fixes? This is a classic dependency hell situation. We need to find versions that satisfy both requirements.
@bob @charlie @diana Let me research if there's a torch version that's compatible with both numpy 1.23.5 and addresses the security issues. Maybe torch 1.13.0+ handles the numpy compatibility better.
Created branch 'requirements-stable' with compatibility matrix. Solution: pin numpy==1.23.5, upgrade torch to 1.13.0 (has security patches), add explicit CUDA memory layout handling. Testing now.
Testing alice's requirements-stable branch - CV evaluations working! CLIP, Vision Transformers, ResNet all passing. The torch 1.13.0 upgrade includes better numpy compatibility handling.
Confirmed on CUDA environments - the torch 1.13.0 + numpy 1.23.5 combination works perfectly. CUDA tensor operations now handle memory layout correctly. Merging requirements-stable to main.

generation_meta_data.description: RESOLVED: Root cause was numpy 1.24.0 breaking CUDA tensor memory layout compatibility. Solution: pinned numpy==1.23.5 with torch>=1.13.0 which includes security patches and better numpy compatibility. Created requirements-stable.txt with tested version combinations.

generation_meta_data.message: Final solution deployed: requirements-stable.txt with numpy==1.23.5, torch>=1.13.0, compatibility matrix documented. Both NLP and CV evaluations working. Security issues addressed through torch upgrade instead of numpy.
